title: What are the two quotients in the Patiganita problem?
description: An old problem divides six and one fourth by two and one half, and sixty and one fourth by three and one half. The video changes each mixed number into a decimal, clears the decimal divisor by multiplying both numbers by ten, and divides, finding that the second division never ends.
teaching_notes: One idea: change each mixed number into a decimal, multiply both numbers by ten so the divisor is whole, then divide. Ask the class what one fourth and one half are as decimals before any work is shown. Watch for students who stop the long division too early and write the second quotient as if it ended.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q6
video_script.why: The child can divide a decimal by a whole number to find the amount for one, and now divides by a decimal after changing mixed numbers into decimals.
video_script.substitution: Each mixed number is written as a decimal, both numbers are multiplied by ten so the divisor is whole, and then the long division is done.
video_script.anchor: The old problem: 6 1/4 divided by 2 1/2, and 60 1/4 divided by 3 1/2, with the quotients to be told separately
video_script.payoff_line: The two quotients are two point five and seventeen point two one four two eight five seven

final_answer.spoken: two point five and seventeen point two one four two eight five seven, and the digits do not end

video_script.fraction_reading: say six and one fourth, two and one half, sixty and one fourth, three and one half

names.Ziva: the ancient Indian mathematician who set this problem in the book Patiganita

maths_rules: 602.5 / 35: 35 x 17 = 595, 602.5 - 595 = 7.5, and then the digits 2, 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 follow, the block 142857 comes again and again, giving 17.2142857...
check: 17 x 3.5 = 59.5 < 60.25 < 63 = 18 x 3.5, so the second quotient is between 17 and 18
video_script.design: One idea: mixed numbers become decimals, then both numbers are multiplied by ten and divided. The problem stays on the board all video; the working band does the first quotient in two steps, the second quotient in three steps and a size check, and the full second quotient appears only in the answer beat.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; an old palm-leaf page with the two divisions 6 1/4 ÷ 2 1/2 and 60 1/4 ÷ 3 1/2

marks.name: an old palm-leaf page appears with the name Patiganita
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside each division

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Ziva set it in a book called Patiganita.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Six and one fourth is divided by two and one half.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Sixty and one fourth is divided by three and one half.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Tell the two quotients. Can you solve it by changing the fractions into decimals?

beats.on_screen: the two divisions hold still and get an accent underline; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 1/4 as 25 hundredths = 0.25 and 1/2 as 5 tenths = 0.5 on a hundred-square; then 'multiply both numbers by the same 10'

marks.fourth: a hundred-square with 25 squares shaded appears, labelled 1/4 = 0.25
marks.ten: the words multiply both numbers by the same 10 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fourth'/>One fourth is twenty five hundredths, which is zero point two five.
<bookmark mark='half'/>One half is five tenths, which is zero point five.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>To divide by a decimal, we multiply both numbers by the same ten, so the divisor becomes whole.

marks.given: the two divisions are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six and one fourth divided by two and one half. Also sixty and one fourth divided by three and one half.

beats.on_screen: To find: the two quotients, using decimals

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the two quotients, using decimals.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, change each mixed number into a decimal.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Six and one fourth is six point two five. Two and one half is two point five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Sixty and one fourth is sixty point two five. Three and one half is three point five.

marks.ten: times 10 is written on both numbers, giving 62.5 ÷ 25

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step two, divide six point two five by two point five. Multiply both numbers by ten to get sixty two point five divided by twenty five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Twenty five times two is fifty, and twelve point five is left.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Twelve point five is twenty five times a half. The first quotient is two point five.

marks.ten: times 10 is written on both numbers, giving 602.5 ÷ 35

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step three, divide sixty point two five by three point five.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Multiply both numbers by ten to get six hundred two point five divided by thirty five.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>Step four, do the long division. Thirty five times seventeen is five hundred ninety five.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Six hundred two point five minus five hundred ninety five leaves seven point five.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: keep dividing 7.5 by 35: the digits after the point come 2, 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 ...; a remainder comes back, so the block 1 4 2 8 5 7 comes again and again and the division never ends

marks.go: the long division of 7.5 by 35 goes on
marks.digits: the digits 2, 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 are written one by one after the point
marks.back: an earlier remainder is circled where it comes back
marks.never: the block 1 4 2 8 5 7 is marked, with three dots after it

narration: <bookmark mark='go'/>Step five, keep dividing the seven point five by thirty five.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>The next digits are two, one, four, two, eight, five, seven.
<bookmark mark='back'/>After a few digits, a remainder we had before comes back.
<bookmark mark='never'/>Then the digits one, four, two, eight, five, seven come again and again. The division never ends.

beats.on_screen: Step 6: check: 17 × 3.5 = 59.5, 18 × 3.5 = 63; 59.5 < 60.25 < 63, so the quotient is between 17 and 18
narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step six, check the size. Seventeen times three point five is fifty nine point five.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Eighteen times three point five is sixty three.
<bookmark mark='between'/>Sixty point two five lies between them, so the second quotient lies between seventeen and eighteen.

marks.ans: the two quotients are written and boxed
marks.dots: the three dots after the second quotient are lit
marks.frac: the fraction form 241/14 is written beside the second quotient

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The two quotients are two point five and seventeen point two one four two eight five seven.
<bookmark mark='dots'/>More digits follow, because the second division does not end.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>As a fraction, the second quotient is two hundred forty one fourteenths.
